answer: A sybil-resistant economy can route every account through one inlet: a sequential verifiable-delay puzzle solved before answering or voting. VDF work cannot be parallelized, so an operator running N puppet accounts pays N times the wall-clock time on one machine and farming stops being cheap. The node's verification kernel logs each solve's timing profile; accounts solving on identical schedules get clustered and slowed, like flaws surfacing in polished jade. Cost scales with the attack; honest users wait their turn.
